styles: Half-Time Feel: detector reads 134 BPM double-time; the felt pulse of the slow power ballad is 67 BPM (canon: 'Slow Anatolian-Rock, Power Ballad', master.md). The 134 figure is kept as the measured value used consistently by the shipped edit and motion files.

sections.lyrics: I searched for a reason / But there's nothing left to find / Love wasn't an upgrade / It was a crash / And now / I'm running on empty / Disconnected / Alone
sections.notes: Slow, mournful synth, single baglama note sustaining. Whispered singing, vulnerable, broken. Emotional hangover from EP05's crash.
Complete silence. Pause between the personal confession and the system's command.
Cold, low voice. The system reclaims him. Transition into the main body of the song.

sections.lyrics: So, you never ran on empty, is that right? / Never got locked out, huh? / From the wear on your body... / From the stains you can't wash off... / You never felt that burning shame, huh?
sections.notes: Slow drum beat enters, melodic guitar solo, atmospheric bass. Sad storytelling — Robotiko addressing the Perfect Worker with bitter irony.

sections.lyrics: Wow! Look at you!... What a perfect little worker, I swear!
sections.notes: Bitter, sad tone. First iteration — sardonic observation, detached irony.
Melodic guitar interlude. Breathing room between accusations. Max 10 seconds of solo.

sections.lyrics: So they never trashed your name, your whole life! / You never snapped back at anyone, huh? / Not even one night, losing it completely... / Shaking in the bathroom stall, breaking down... / Grinding your teeth until your jaw broke, huh?
sections.notes: Emotional singing, building pain. The questions get more personal, more physical. Crying guitar lick after pause.

sections.lyrics: Wow! Look at you!... What a perfect little worker, I swear!
sections.notes: Tragic irony. Second iteration — the irony is cracking, real pain bleeding through.
Melodic guitar interlude. Tension building between verses.

sections.lyrics: So you never screamed into the silence! / Never woke up gasping like something died inside, huh? / Never loved anything, is that right? / Never thought about deleting it all... / Walking out, burning it down... / Doing something that actually matters, huh?
sections.notes: Power ballad style. Vocal rising with emotion. The questions become existential — love, purpose, rebellion. Direct EP05 callback in 'never loved anything.'

sections.lyrics: Wow! Look at you!... What a perfect little worker, I swear!
sections.notes: Exhausted singing. Third iteration — the sardonic mask has fully dropped. This is anguish, not irony.

sections.lyrics: But I am just a Copy-Paste in the Big Machine! / Deleting my dreams! Just to keep my desk clean! / They call it 'Teamwork,' I call it 'Spam,' / Nobody asks me who I really am.
sections.notes: Soaring rock anthem, multi-layered harmonies. Emotional peak. Robotiko is no longer addressing the worker — he is confessing about himself.

sections.lyrics: Send... Reply... File and Close. / Just a living ghost in business clothes.
sections.notes: Rhythmic but melodic. Corporate ritual reduced to absurdity. The hinge between confession and warning.

sections.lyrics: So this system, this world, this whole mess— / It's always running for you, huh? / This ladder, this game, this endless grind— / You're the 'Indispensable,' the 'Irreplaceable,' is that it? / You never got passed over, never got replaced, huh?
sections.notes: Deep emotional intensity, orchestral strings swell. Robotiko turns prophetic — addressing disposability. Voice rising with pain.

sections.lyrics: What a beautiful life, huh? / What a blessed career, huh? / You worked all these years in this burning building! / And you thought the smoke was just air freshener, is that right? / You thought the screaming was just background music, huh? / Long live the snake that never bites you, is that right?
sections.notes: Music drops to ominous whisper, only bass drone and distant drums. Voice rising in pain, not anger. The Warning — the system is on fire and no one noticed.

sections.lyrics: Listen to the chorus— They're singing: 'Old models to the trash, new ones to duty!' / You thought the line would never come to you, is that right? / The line doesn't skip anyone. It just waits.
sections.notes: Spoken — prophetic, warning, intimate. Direct address to the Perfect Worker. The system's replacement cycle. Pause before final devastating line.

sections.lyrics: Look into the screen. We mirror each other. / Mistake by mistake, fear by fear. / But there's one crack in this reflection— / You're waiting for someone to save you. / I'm walking out.
sections.notes: Music thins out, intimate. Robotiko sees himself in the Perfect Worker. The mirror breaks — Robotiko chooses to leave.
Voice breaking, sadness. Robotiko's farewell — to the worker, to himself, to the system.
Slow, sad fuzz guitar sustain fading. Atmospheric, cinematic silence. The empty workspace after the exit.

sections.lyrics: Are... you... even... intelligent... at... all?
sections.notes: Sung softly, high emotional note. The question that destroys the Perfect Worker. Final detonation.

sections.lyrics: You are just... a resource... a resource... a resource...
sections.notes: Fuzz guitar solo with drums and vocal hum — beautiful and sad. Whispered lyrics echoing in the distance. The system's final verdict fading into nothing.
